title: Vanishing spin stiffness in weakly disordered two-dimensional Heisenberg ferromagnets
authors: Jacopo Niedda, Aldo Coraggio, Giacomo Bracci-Testasecca, Antonello Scardicchio
abstract: We show that a small fraction of antiferromagnetic bonds qualitatively alters the long-wavelength dynamics of two-dimensional Heisenberg ferromagnets. Although the classical ground state remains magnetized, weak bond frustration generates logarithmically correlated spatial fluctuations of the local spin stiffness, despite the microscopic disorder being short ranged. A replica field theory calculation shows that the effective disorder strength grows under coarse graining, while the spin stiffness decreases, yielding anomalously soft magnons with a scale-dependent dynamical exponent $z > 2$. Numerical diagonalization of the semiclassical spin-wave Hamiltonian confirms the anomalous low-energy scaling. The flow is toward an infinite-disorder, zero stiffness regime.
summary: This paper demonstrates that weak bond disorder in 2D Heisenberg ferromagnets fundamentally changes their long-wavelength magnetic dynamics. Using field theory and numerical methods, the authors show this disorder causes the spin stiffness to decay toward zero. This results in anomalous magnon behavior characterized by a dynamical exponent $z > 2$, indicating a transition towards an infinite-disorder regime.
main_problem: The study investigates how weak, short-ranged antiferromagnetic bond disorder qualitatively alters the long-wavelength dynamics of two-dimensional Heisenberg ferromagnets.
main_result: Weak disorder causes the spin stiffness to vanish at long wavelengths, leading to anomalously soft magnons characterized by a dynamical exponent $z > 2$.
method: The analysis employs replica field theory calculations combined with numerical diagonalization of the semiclassical spin-wave Hamiltonian.
model_or_system: The system is a two-dimensional Heisenberg ferromagnet on a square lattice subjected to quenched random bond disorder, modeled by varying exchange couplings $J_{ij}$.
key_observables: Spin stiffness ($ho_s$), dynamical exponent ($z$), and the spatial correlation function of local spin stiffness $C(\vec{x}, \vec{x}')$.
important_parameters: The disorder concentration $p$ (small), the system dimension ($d=2$), and the RG flow parameter $\ell$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the small $p$ approximation and the long-wavelength limit, treating the disorder as marginal in 2D.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the increase of the dynamical exponent $z$ with disorder strength $p$, and show spin stiffness correlations decaying logarithmically with distance.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the disordered Hamiltonian to calculating local stiffness via a twist protocol, then applying replica field theory and RG flow to derive scaling laws for $ho_s$ and $z$.
why_interesting: The finding of anomalous low-energy scaling ($z>2$) due to disorder is relevant to understanding critical dynamics in disordered quantum magnets, which shares theoretical parallels with systems studied in AMO physics.
